blog_summary: Adrian Colyer reviews a 2015 position paper by Ward and De Vault that outlines ten key challenges for highly-interactive dialog systems, with a focus on spoken dialog. The authors categorize these challenges into three main areas: improving power and robustness, reducing development costs, and deepening understanding. Colyer highlights the compelling argument for 'superhuman' dialog systems, which could surpass human performance by leveraging real-time sensing, advanced planning, and cognitive advantages. He also notes the importance of modeling multifunctional behaviors (e.g., backchanneling) and integrating learned and designed behaviors. The paper emphasizes the need for continuous dialog state tracking, compositional behavior specifications, and better evaluation methods. Colyer underscores the disconnect between dialog systems research and social science findings, advocating for more comprehensible models and interdisciplinary collaboration.
paper_title: Ten challenges in highly-interactive dialog systems
paper_abstract: Systems capable of highly-interactive dialog have recently been developed in several domains. This paper considers how to build on these successes to make systems more robust, easier to develop, more adaptable, and more scientifically significant.
